newsitem.title: KENYA: ATHLETICS-KONCHELLAH FAILS IN COMEBACK BID.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-KONCHELLAH FAILS IN COMEBACK BID.

text.p: Former world champion Billy Konchellah's hopes of a major international return were dashed on Friday when the veteran 800 metres runner crashed out of the Kenyan world championship trials.
Konchellah, 35, finished eighth in his semifinal heat and failed to qualify for Saturday's final.
"The younger boys ran so well. It was one of those bad days for me," said Konchellah, who has made a number of successful comebacks during his career.

Konchellah has had nagging knee problems in recent seasons and was forced to pull out the trials for last year's Atlanta Olympics because of injury. But he had hoped to qualify for the world championships in Athens in August.

Konchellah's younger brother Patrick, however, won his semifinal heat convincingly. The Commonwealth champion clocked one minute 45.59 seconds ahead of Olympic bronze medallist Fred Onyancha (1:45.67) and David Kiptoo (1:45.84).
In the 10,000 metres final Paul Koech beat three-times world cross-country champion Paul Tergat into third place.
In a tactical race, Koech burst away during the 18th lap and ran away to finish in 28:20.0. He was followed by Dominic Kirui (28:36.0). Tergat clocked 28:38.1.
Both Koech and Tergat complained about the tight programme at the trials, saying that they had asked the Kenya Amateur Athletics Association to postpone the final until Saturday.
"This made us strain a lot. Running 20 kilometres in two days at altitude will certainly affect my world championship programme," Koech said.
